stories.title: Two men die in separate road crashes overnight
stories.summary: Two people have died in separate road crashes in the country overnight. A man in his 20s has died in a car crash in Co Limerick while a man in his 50s has died in a car crash in Co Meath. In Limerick, the man in his 20s died in a single-vehicle car crash while two passengers in the car were taken to hospital for treatment. The crash occurred on the N21 at Cummeen, Adare, Co Limerick, at around 2.40am. His body was taken to the mortuary at University Hospital Limerick where a post-mortem examination will be carried out in due course. The two passengers, another man aged in his 20s and an adult teenager, were taken to University Hospital Limerick for treatment.

stories.title: Nikita Hand credits mother with saving her life
stories.summary: Nikita Hand, who won a civil case against former MMA fighter Conor McGregor, has credited her mother with saving her life. In November 2024, a jury at the High Court found that Mr McGregor raped Ms Hand in a hotel room in December 2018 and awarded her almost €250,000 in damages. "Anything could have happened to me. Like you know, with the circumstances of what happened, toxic shock syndrome could have happened to me. "She knew I needed medical help, and that's what she did for me. So she saved my life," explained Ms Hand. Ms Hand said that there are now two Nikitas - the woman who existed before the night of her assault and the woman who exists now. "I'm still learning to love the new Nikita, but I'm not quite there yet," she said.

stories.title: Discussions over Ireland's involvement in naval alliance
stories.summary: The head of the Department of Defence's maritime security unit has confirmed that discussions have been held with the UK over Ireland’s involvement in a North Atlantic naval alliance. The UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) is a 10-nation alliance, which also comprises of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden. While Ireland is not looking to join the group itself, it is exploring certain aspects of the partnership, including potential participation in a wider "JEF-Plus" group. JEF is a defence partnership that is focused on rapid response, deterrence, and regional security across Northern Europe. It is not part of NATO, but all members are NATO countries. JEF Plus refers to an extended version of JEF, and Ireland is exploring a potential observer role within this grouping. Dr Margaret Stanley heads the maritime security unit, which was set up at the Department of Defence in late 2024, and was tasked with examining ways to address maritime threats and risks to Ireland.

stories.title: Bonds, rising yields and global sell offs explained
stories.summary: Recent headlines have been highlighting global bond sell offs. Since the Middle East conflict and surging oil prices, global interest rates are rising to curb inflation. Higher interest rates can cause bond selloffs as bond prices go down when interest rates go up. New bonds pay more, so when interest rates rise new bonds are issued with higher payouts. As a result, older existing bonds with older interest payments become less appealing to investors. Sellers need to drop their prices to attract investors to buy older bonds thus creating a bond sell-off.

stories.title: Russia reports cyberattacks on second day of vote
stories.summary: Russia has said that its electronic voting system in Moscow had been hit by "powerful" cyberattacks overnight, as tightly-controlled parliamentary elections entered a second day. Ella Pamfilova, chair of Russia's Central Election Commission, did not give details on the nature of the attack or who was responsible. Russian President Vladimir Putin yesterday accused Ukraine of trying to "hinder" the vote, an accusation to which Kyiv has not responded. Ukraine has called the election farcical. Only parties that support Mr Putin and the Kremlin's military campaign have been registered to run, while voting is also being held in areas of east Ukraine under Russian occupation. "All night long, the Moscow system was subjected to a very powerful, continuous attack," Ms Pamfilova was quoted as saying by Russia's state RIA news agency. "This attack is ongoing -- it is happening practically non-stop," she said.

stories.title: Leitrim's Casey ready for more after faithfulness tested
stories.summary: No word of a lie, Donal Casey's life has changed utterly in the past 12 months. A year ago this weekend, the then 23-year-old was in game mode, an interested spectator in the crowd as the Leitrim SFC quarter-finals were playing out. Nothing really mattered at that time apart from a manic determination to help Leitrim Gaels, who had safely navigated a path to the semi-finals, get their hands on the Fenagh Perpetual Cup for the first time in the club’s history. Life's most valuable information in that moment was finding out who would be facing Mal Guckian’s side in the last four. He did help his club to that coveted silverware, but life isn’t just about football anymore. After what happened in that county final, his outlook changed forever. Back to that 2025 county final though and the victory over Sean O’Heslin’s. It was a day when dreams should have been realised, but for the young centre half-back, it came so close to complete tragedy.

stories.title: Dunne doubts there's appetite for more GAA rule changes
stories.summary: Former Offaly forward Nigel Dunne has questioned whether there is a sufficient appetite amongst the GAA public for further rule changes in Gaelic football. Several tweaks will be trialled over the coming months in third level Ryan Cup fixtures, following research and discussion amongst members of the Expert Advisory Group, which is chaired by former Mayo player and manager Kevin McStay. The EAG - which was formed following the work of the Football Review Committee - is charged with monitoring trends in the game and has come up with a number of proposals to be introduced in the coming months. Among the key proposals is the banning of fisted points (unless the ball is already in flight), limiting the number of consecutive handpasses to three and awarding four points for a goal. A backcourt rule, whereby the ball cannot return back over the halfway line, and a modified kickout rule, where the ball is no longer required to travel beyond the two-point arc, are also included in the slate of changes. "In isolation they're fine and I don’t disagree with them but the problem is why change now?

stories.title: WSL wrap: Wins for Chelsea and London City Lionesses
stories.summary: Chelsea and London City Lionesses climbed to second and third in the Women's Super League table with respective victories over Birmingham and Charlton. After thumping Manchester United 5-0 last weekend, Chelsea won again as Lexi Potter and Melvine Malard secured a 2-0 win. Potter found the roof of the net in the eighth minute and in the 71st minute France star Malard made a quick impact from the bench with her first goal at Stamford Bridge. Republic of Ireland captain Katie McCabe was on the Chelsea bench, coming on after 86 minutes in place of Alyssa Thompson. London City lost 2-1 to West Ham last time out but kept in touch with leaders Manchester City with a 4-1 triumph at promoted Charlton. Isobel Goodwin’s brace had London City two goals ahead after 15 minutes and, despite Jodie Hutton halving the deficit in the 39th minute with a fine finish, Jana Fernandez restored their advantage before half-time.

stories.title: Adams Verling set for debut in Ireland's WXV opener
stories.summary: Connacht's Jemima Adams Verling will make her Ireland debut in Sunday’s WXV Global Series meeting with the USA in Tallaght. The back row is named at blindside flanker by head coach Scott Bemand for the first game of this five-match Test window, one of four changes from the side that began the Six Nations win against Scotland in May. The 20-year-old played a key role in Ireland’s successful U21 Women’s Six Nations Championship earlier this year, scoring tries against Wales and England, and replaces Brittany Hogan, who is named among the replacements. Beibhinn Parsons hasn’t been included, with the winger still on the comeback from an injury picked up ahead of the Vodafone Women’s Interprovincial championship, with Vicky Elmes Kinlan starting on the right wing and Anna McGann on the bench. Niamh O’Dowd comes in at loosehead prop following the retirement of Ellena Perry, and joins Clíodhna Moloney MacDonald and Linda Djougang in the front row, with Neve Jones, Sadhbh McGrath and Eilís Cahill the replacement trio. Dorothy Wall is the other change from Ireland’s last starting team as she comes in for the injured Sam Monaghan, partnering Fiona Tuite-O'Sullivan (above) in the second row.

stories.title: New Irish Writing: The Most Normal Woman by Roisín Kiberd
stories.summary: We present an extract from The Most Normal Woman, the new essay collection by Roisin Kiberd. In her new collection of essays, Roisin Kiberd explores the many ways we change ourselves in pursuit of perfection – or simply normality – and the toll it takes on our inner lives. Weaving critical commentary with personal experience, she explores Botox, blondeness, exercise addiction, and subcultures including the underground drag scene and competitive dog shows to better understand how beauty is judged and defined. In 2017, on something of a whim, I found myself in Hong Kong, staying at a flat down the street from the Night Market. One evening I set out, past shops with cats in the windows, restaurants selling family-size hot pots and their stranger, smaller cousin, the hot pot for one, past cafes inexplicably dedicated to perfecting the art of making toast, to a tunnel-shaped street lit with neon, hoardings over everything, sunglasses and belts and shoes and wallets and, of course, handbags, sprawled out on displays, with rapid-talking vendors shouting over each other. I'm the type to find the automated cash registers at Tesco overwhelming; the Night Market in Hong Kong was sensory overload, pulling me in, as though the only way out was to locate the replica handbag I was looking for. I’d seen it mostly on Instagram, on the arm of a paranormally long-legged blonde woman I followed who lived in LA. The Givenchy Antigona is still in production now, a black leather tote with short handles and a weird, angular flap on top that doesn’t actually open. Like a lot of Riccardo Tisci-era Givenchy (his reign began in 2005, and ended in 2017) it has a severe, Catholic look to it that I now associate with mid-career Kanye. I walked past rows of bags, some of them dreadful, some of them accurate, some of them decoys for much more accurate bags, hidden upstairs in the buildings behind the stalls. After a while a combination of tiredness and hunger set in –I’d been living on SkyFlakes crackers and canned iced coffee for much of this trip – and I told myself I’d found a good enough vendor. I got talking to an extremely enthusiastic young woman, who led me into a corridor behind the stall and presented me with a catalogue of bags.

"The shutters closed around me and I was devastated, absolutely, completely devastated. "I put my heart and soul into that thing. I really worked very, very hard."

stories.title: OMMA founder on building a 'secret forest' cafe in wartorn Kyiv
stories.summary: Nastya Kharytonova, the Dublin-based Ukrainian founder of OMMA matcha café, speaks to Charlotte Ryan from Kyiv about endurance and inspiration, as she prepares to open the second branch of her business in the Ukrainian capital. The night after I spoke with Kharytonova about her plans to open a Kyiv branch of the café, the warehouse that had built all the dreamy, ethereal and highly specific furniture for the project was destroyed in an air attack. It was a close call for the team, as they had already moved the furniture from the warehouse, but one of many. In the weeks leading up to the launch of OMMA's new space in collaboration with Ukrainian loungewear brand LONDI, the facade of a building 200 metres from their new office was destroyed by a drone. Kharytonova recalls being in the city centre as it happened, seeing the drone "above my head, and then you hear the explosion the second after". OMMA's new opening coincided with a change of tactics by the Russian army over the end of the summer, as it increased daytime assaults, on top of continuing to batter Ukrainian cities at night.

stories.summary: Garda representative bodies and opposition politicians have called for an inquiry with the Association of Garda Sergeants and Inspectors, saying that they have "serious concerns around the independence of the protected disclosures process" within the garda force. The former Minister for Justice also insisted she will not consider her position at Cabinet in light of the revelations contained within the broadcast. Speaking at a Fine Gael conference for small businesses in Dublin today, Ms McEntee reiterated on a number of occasions her position from the Dáil on Thursday that she had "adhered to the law at all times" when it came to protected disclosures during her time at the Department of Justice. "That's a matter for the Minister for Justice, that's not for me to decide," said the Meath East TD when asked should there be a public inquiry into the issues. "My understanding is he's [Jim O'Callaghan] made a decision on that this morning [not to hold an inquiry] so I'm not going to cross over that," she added. On calls for urgent action to ensure the protected disclosure process within An Garda Síochána is independent, Ms McEntee again refrained from offering a viewpoint, saying it was a matter for the Minister for Justice.

stories.title: Minister accused of protected disclosure 'incompetence'
stories.summary: Labour TD Alan Kelly has accused Minister Helen McEntee of either "incompetence or a mistake" in her handling of a protected disclosure, adding that it is something that will "haunt" her and the Government in which she served. Speaking during Leaders' Questions in the Dáil, Deputy Kelly accused Ms McEntee - when she was Minister for Justice - of having "acted without legal authority" by having "revealed Brian O'Reilly's identity, thereby depriving him of the legal protections he was entitled to and exposing the nature of his allegations". Deputy Kelly was taking issue with the minister's decision to direct that the investigation of Brian O'Reilly's protected disclosure "be removed from your Secretary General and be redirected to An Garda Siochána, thereby usurping the OPDC statutory direction, which is their role". He said that the minister had "directly interfered with a serious and significant protective disclosure" and brought about consequences that were "detrimental to Brian O'Reilly's life, his career, his livelihood and well-being of him, his wife, his children, his family". The Labour TD said that he did not believe she had acted deliberately, and so must have acted out of "incompetence or a mistake". Minister McEntee, who was taking Leaders' Questions, rejected the deputy's claims.

"Our members have responded to the Government's failure to grasp the core issue on a new public service pay agreement," said Fórsa National Secretary Richy Carrothers. "In its failure to address pay issues at the commencement of talks, the Government has made this industrial action inevitable," Mr Carrothers said. Earlier, it was announced that primary school teachers, who are members of the INTO, are to begin industrial action next month over delays in agreeing a new public sector pay deal. The previous deal expired on 30 June, and formal talks have yet to begin on a successor agreement.

stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has signed a bill authorising new sanctions designed to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine, shortly after it received congressional approval this week. The legislation takes aim at Russia's energy and defence sectors, alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials. The measures also target Moscow's 'shadow fleet' of tankers used to evade western sanctions and give Mr Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. Critics say the legislation gives President Trump the power to impose levies ⁠that ‌could last well beyond his presidency. Some opposed to the bill also say Mr Trump already has the authority he needs to impose sanctions on Russia but has chosen not to do so. The legislation will also target companies and foreign actors supporting Russia's military and extend sanctions involving Iran.

stories.title: Carter-Vickers: Celtic have chance to flip the narrative
stories.summary: Cameron Carter-Vickers believes the negative narrative around Celtic can change against Rangers at an all-green Parkhead on Sunday. Martin O'Neill and his players are in the firing line after a comprehensive 3-0 Premier Sports Cup defeat at Ibrox last Sunday was followed by a 3-1 loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League opener at Parkhead on Thursday night. Despite a flawless start to the defence of their William Hill Premiership title – six wins from six games – there have been rumblings of discontent around the Parkhead club since Celtic were knocked out of the Champions League play-off by Austrian side LASK on a 5-4 aggregate after being 4-0 up at one stage in the tie and this week has intensified the scrutiny. Due to a ticket allocation spat between the two city rivals which saw the authorities step in, there were only Gers fans inside Ibrox and there will only be Hoops supporters in the 60,000-capacity Celtic Park at the weekend. The 28-year-old United States centre-back believes the opportunity is "100 per cent" available to restore a feelgood factor in the league game against Derek McInnes’ side. "We want to come out on Sunday, with the crowd behind us and everyone together and try to put a performance together that will get the result we want.

stories.title: Gleeson calls time on Waterford career at the age of 31
stories.summary: Waterford's Austin Gleeson has announced his retirement from inter-county hurling, bringing an end to a Déise senior career that began in 2014. Gleeson, now 31, was part of the Waterford side that contested the 2017 and 2020 All-Ireland finals, this after he was named both Hurler of the Year and Young Hurler of the Year in 2016. A year previous, the Mount Sion clubman collected senior silverware after his county got the better of Cork in the Division 1 league final. There was also All-Ireland success, with a minor medal won in 2013 and an Under-21 victory three years later. After opting out of the Waterford set-up in 2024, Gleeson returned and was part of the squad during Peter Queally's two years at the helm, though he did not see any championship action, with injuries curtailing the forward's involvement. Gleeson's decision, perhaps, is not surprising, given the signals he was getting earlier this year. Speaking on Off The Ball, he said: "I'm done now. I knew it at the start of 2026. There was one training session I remember in particular where it didn't go the best. It was 23 December; we trained down in Passage.

stories.title: Iraola calls on Liverpool to be ruthless at Bournemouth
stories.summary: Andoni Iraola is looking forward to returning to Bournemouth with Liverpool – even if the opponents may understand his methods better than his own players. The Spaniard is six games into his reign as Liverpool manager after leaving the Cherries, whom he guided into Europe for the first time at the end of last season. His new side are unbeaten so far, although performances have been mixed. That record will be put to the test as Liverpool travel to the Vitality Stadium in the Premier League on Sunday, and Iraola admits it will be a strange feeling. He said: "On the personal side I am really looking forward to meeting them, to hug them. They are players that I love, staff that I worked with and appreciate so much. "I was buzzing for them when they played their first European game. I wish them all the best but there is another part – and that is the most important one – that we need to go there and win and be as ruthless as possible, and leave all the talk for after the game.

stories.title: Nankivell: ' I would love to stay here at Munster'
stories.summary: Munster centre Alex Nankivell has confessed his wishes to remain in Ireland and with the province for the foreseeable, as he heads into his fourth season at the club, and a contract year. The former Chiefs back joined up with the province in Autumn of 2023, and has been a shining light since his arrival, culminating in winning Munster player of the year for the 2025/26 season. Now 29, Nankivell has thoroughly enjoyed his time in Ireland and would be keen to stay on, and potentially line out in green. "I would love to stay here at Munster", he told reporters on Wednesday. "It is definitely in the back of my mind, particularly coming off contract after this season. "I guess the thing about if I re-sign, international rugby is the pinnacle, in my opinion. I've had dreams to play for the All Blacks, and I didn't really think about it when I came over as I didn't think the opportunity would present itself to become Irish-qualified being here, but now it kind of does.

stories.title: Jarvis Cocker - Oasis show was like a 'religious rally'
stories.summary: Jarvis Cocker has said attending an Oasis concert during their recent world tour was like a "religious rally" with "many more fans". The 62-year-old Common People singer was amazed by the Britpop group and the masses who turned up to see them live last year for their reunion Oasis Live ’25 world tour. Cocker attended one of the group’s shows at London’s Wembley stadium with his son, where he realised the band - led by brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher - had "many more fans" than Pulp. Speaking at a press conference, Cocker said the show came a day after Pulp performed what he thought was "quite a big concert" - only to be struck by the crowd that gathered for Oasis. He added: "It’s the first time that I’ve watched a show from the guest area, so you were surrounded by the crowd on all sides. "I’d never come across an atmosphere like that at a concert before.

stories.title: Escalation fears in Middle East as Houthis attack Riyadh
stories.summary: The United States warned yesterday that hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis could "escalate rapidly" after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. US President Donald Trump cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House yesterday. The White House gave no explanation for the early return, which comes as a new threshold was crossed in the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen and are fighting government forces backed by a coalition led by Riyadh. Loud explosions rang out twice yesterday in the Saudi capital, where AFP journalists saw a fuel tank bearing the logo of oil giant Aramco on fire near the airport. "This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly," the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should "seriously reconsider travel to and through the region". The Houthis's lightning offensive seizing swathes of Yemeni territory in recent weeks has left hundreds dead and, according to the UN, displaced more than 110,000 people.

stories.summary: A number of trade unions and political activists marched in Dublin, calling for action on housing and the cost of living ahead of Budget 2027. SIPTU, Unite, Fórsa, and others gathered at the Garden of Remembrance to walk to Leinster House where a rally took place. Political parties such as People Before Profit, Solidarity, Sinn Féin and the Social Democrats were among those present. "The central contradiction in Ireland today is that we have a wealthy economy but the workers who create that wealth are being priced out of a decent life," SIPTU Sector Organiser Paddy Cole said before the protest. He added: "Whether people rent or hope to buy, too much of their wages is swallowed by housing. Workers from home and abroad can have qualifications, full-time jobs and good wages, yet still be unable to leave the family home, rent a decent place to live or plan for children. "That is an abject policy failure, not a failure of the people who are trying to do all the right things. This crisis unites healthcare assistants, retail workers, civil servants, hospitality workers, construction workers, transport workers and many others. Governments respond when people organise and put them under pressure."

stories.title: Man charged in Michael Healy-Rae assault investigation
stories.summary: A man in his 50s has been charged in relation to the investigation into an assault on Kerry TD Michael Healy-Rae in Dublin on Wednesday afternoon. He is due to appear before a sitting of Dublin District Court at the Criminal Courts of Justice today at 10.30am. Mr Healy-Rae was travelling in his own vehicle on Cork Street in Dublin city at around 4.10pm on Wednesday when he was approached by a man who assaulted him through the window of his car. Following the assault, the Kerry TD was taken from the road by gardaí who were quickly on the scene. They took him to Kevin Street Garda Station and an ambulance was called. He attended St Vincent's University Hospital for his injuries, and was discharged around 9pm on Wednesday night, having needed stitches for injuries to his face and mouth.

stories.title: OPW approves €566,666 for coastal protection in Rosslare
stories.summary: The Office of Public Works (OPW) has announced the approval of €566,666 following an application by Wexford County Council's for funding under the OPW's Minor Flood Mitigation Works and Coastal Protection Scheme. The Council will use the funding to provide rock revetment coastal protection fronting at Kelly’s Resort Hotel in Rosslare. The hotel was first established along Rosslare Strand in 1895 and now employs more than 250 people. Minister of State Kevin "Boxer" Moran announced the funding approval, while the commencement and progression of any works will be announced by Wexford County Council. Earlier this year, Chief Executive of Wexford County Council Eddie Taaffe said the existing coastal defences along Rosslare Strand were damaged and needed to be repaired urgently. Rosslare residents have expressed fear that their properties will not survive another winter, due to the worsening impacts of coastal erosion and storms of increasing frequency and severity.

stories.title: Death toll rises to 31 in Pakistan police HQ bomb attack
stories.summary: The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan has risen to at least 31, according to local officials. "At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and more than 100 injured so far in the militant attack," the official said, adding that fighting was ongoing. Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex at Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, on Friday afternoon. Attackers rammed a car carrying explosives into the police facility as officers and their families were praying in a mosque, officials said. Local militant group Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a faction linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, the Pakistani Taliban, has claimed responsibility for the attack. The police compound serves as a district-level police headquarters, housing key offices of the Counter Terrorism Department, Special Branch and several other police units.

stories.title: Townsend emerges unscathed after pitch roller incident
stories.summary: Former England winger Andros Townsend has joked Stoke away "wasn't so bad after all" following a bizarre incident in Thailand where he was run over by a pitch roller. Ex-Tottenham and Crystal Palace attacker Townsend currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media which showed the 35-year-old being taken out ahead of a fixture at Pattani. Townsend was warming up when a member of staff at Pattani appeared to lose control of the pitch roller and it crashed into the 13-cap England international. The left leg of the Prachuap player briefly got stuck under the vehicle, but he did feature off the bench late on in the 3-0 win. Regular ITV pundit Townsend later took to Instagram to make light of the incident, referencing one of his recent posts in which he contrasted a sun-drenched Thai away trip with previous visits to Stoke’s windswept bet365 Stadium. Townsend said on his Instagram story: "It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad after all. Swipe to see why." Another post described Townsend as 'The King of Memes in Thai League history’ and he replied "trust me" with four laughing emojis.
